chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Petty theft at the House and keeping the project going
summary: They sort out a baseball-bat theft case, and she is satisfied with how the neighborhood kids behave.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: All right, we're back now after a short interruption, we've been sorting out a case of petty larceny at the House that Jazz Built.
Yeah, things are beginning to show up one at a time. That was Fifi, Mary's dog, I think Fifi wanted to get into the act, too.
Do you just want to say a sentence or two about the case of -- just to give a sense of the kind things you have to put up with running a project like this in South Bronx.
Well, we found out when I came in here, Buddy said that there were a few little things missing, like his camera and some nails and a frisbee and a hammer and a basketball --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Yeah, a baseball bat and so we began looking around and I found that the fire extinguisher was not where it usually is, so Buddy sort of spread out a rumor that he was going to give a little reward for the stuff if it showed up. One boy came and said he had the stuff at his house but he had found it and he implicated another little boy, saying that the other little boy had taken the stuff, but this turned out not to be true so we sent for his mother, so what we've done now, we've put out a little notice if anything shows up and it looks like it might have come from the House that Jazz Built, you know, we'd appreciate their cooperation in turning it back.

And so far, I mean I'm very satisfied with the fact that the kids are going to cooperate. We finally found the fire extinguisher over here in the next little courtyard. I don't know whether it's still working or not but I suppose it needs recharging; they just played with it, I just hope no kids was hurt.
